welcome.title: ACAB Fort File Analyzer
welcome.lead:
Isotope analysis tool for ACAB simulations.
Load the fort.6 and inp.5 files from multiple simulations
and visualise the activity, comparison tables and a detailed report of the selected isotope.
welcome.howto:
• Enter the path of the folder that contains the simulation subfolders.
  • Each subfolder must contain at least one fort.6 file.
  • To read Tirr, Tcool and flux automatically, include inp.5 in each subfolder.
  • Optionally, upload a YAML configuration file with half-lives and figures.
  • Click Analyze.

metrics.title: {n}. Production-Optimisation Metrics of {label}
metrics.sat_desc: A<sub>theo</sub>(t) = A<sub>sat</sub>·(1−e<sup>−λt</sup>) during irradiation, anchored to the ACAB value at the end of T<sub>irr</sub>. Times to reach 50/75/90/95 % of saturation and whether they fit within the current irradiation.
metrics.rend_desc: Mean activity produced per hour of irradiation (A<sub>peak</sub>/T<sub>irr</sub>) versus the rate of the last 10 % of the irradiation tramo — answers whether it still pays off to keep irradiating.
metrics.pureza_desc: P = A(target isotope) / Σ A(isotopes considered) at the peak instant, expressed in %. By default the isotopes of the same element present in the fort.6 are considered (after radiochemical separation the product contains only that element).
metrics.pureza_tooltip: Default criterion: isotopes of the same target element (e.g. for I131: I130, I132, I133… whichever are present in the fort.6). Editable via the checklist below.
metrics.pureza_nodo_comun_note: The table below evaluates each simulation at ITS OWN peak (not comparable across cases if the peaks don't tie). The CSV export evaluates ALL simulations at the common node: the INTERSECTION of the peak plateaus, if it exists (labelled "peak", a genuine maximum for all of them) or, otherwise, a reference common instant (labelled "common instant", never "peak"), declared with its time origin in the file header.
metrics.pureza_csv_meta_pico: all simulations evaluated at t = {t} h ({origen}) — common MAXIMUM node (peak) of the loaded simulations
metrics.pureza_csv_meta_instante_comun: all simulations evaluated at t = {t} h ({origen}) — NO common maximum node among the loaded simulations (non-overlapping plateaus); reference common instant, NOT the peak of all of them
metrics.csv_meta_interseccion: (INTERSECTION: {n} instants from {ini} to {fin} h, the minimum was used)
metrics.origen_fin_irradiacion: from the end of irradiation / EOI
metrics.pureza_na: no t<sub>peak</sub> or total activity is zero.
metrics.pureza_serie_desc: P(t) = A({label}, t) / Σ A(isotopes considered, t) at each cooling step (t = 0 = end of irradiation), with the 99.9 % pharmaceutical threshold and the instant it is crossed. Uses the same isotope list as the section above.
metrics.pureza_serie_cruce_label: Minimum cooling time for pharmaceutical quality
metrics.pureza_serie_no_alcanzado: Threshold not reached within the simulated cooling window
metrics.pureza_serie_aviso_no_monotono: Warning: P(t) drops back below the threshold at t = {t} h (P = {p} %).
metrics.aesp_desc: A(target, t) divided by the TOTAL mass of iodine present (stable + long-lived + radioactive, every iodine isotope in the fort.6). Stable I-127 and long-lived I-129 do not affect radionuclidic purity, but they dilute the product: the same becquerels spread over more grams of iodine. Same time domain as P(t).
metrics.aesp_na: no cooling data, or not applicable to this isotope (iodine only).
metrics.aesp_sin_destacado: no purity crossing instant to highlight.
metrics.aesp_csv_meta_sim: {sim}: carrier-free ceiling = {techo} MBq/g | highlighted value at t_cross = {destacado} MBq/g (t = {tcruce} h)

chains.title: Chain contribution analysis
chains.scope_note: Quantifies, for the target isotope IFINAL, the contribution of each initial isotope of the target (R_i) and of each reaction chain within it (Y_z_i = R_i·X_z_i). Requires an analysis already generated (and at least partially run) from the "Chain analysis" section of the ACAB INP File Configurator — load the root folder of that analysis here, independent of the simulations folder above.
chains.root_required: Enter the analysis folder before loading.
chains.reference_note: Each chain's probability P (CHAINS output) depends on the tapes (fort.22/fort.24) generated from THIS reference folder's spectrum — the same INITIAL/IFINAL/NMAX/PCNT can give different P values with a different reference. Verified example: TE130→I131 gives P=95.79/3.12/1.09% with the original fixture family's tapes and P=94.550/4.303/1.144% with the v.5 reference's tapes (thesis spectrum) — do not compare CHAINS figures across analyses with different references.
chains.cobertura_completa: Full coverage: every isotope in the reference's initial inventory is selected — Σ R_i ≈ 1 is the Bateman linearity control (deviation = numerical rounding + tail dropped by PCNT).
chains.cobertura_parcial: Partial coverage: {n} of {total} initial-inventory isotopes selected — Σ R_i represents only that fraction, ≈ 1 is not expected.
chains.tabla2_title: Table 2 — contribution by chain (Y_z,i), descending order
chains.ptot_note: PTOT is the TOTAL probability that the initial isotope ends up as the target isotope — it varies (it can be ≈100% or much lower, depending on how much of the initial isotope actually reaches IFINAL), not a fixed normalisation. Each chain's % (P) IS normalised to 100 among the returned chains, so X_z,i = P/100 holds either way; Σ_z Y_z,i can fall below R_i if some chains below PCNT are not detailed.
chains.row_hint: Select a row in table 2 to see that chain's diagram.
